answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 101 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The yarrow graph is validated at intake and the inlet frontier is published, and thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and crystal anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Honest users pay that once, farms 25 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
